title: Infinitely many graph manifolds with unique geometrical piece that admit arbitrarily many Anosov flows
summary: Anosov flows have a long and rich history, firstly motivated by the study of geodesic flows in negative curvature surface by Anosov and Sinai. Not every closed manifold admits an Anosov flow for well-known reasons: the fundamental group of a 3-manifold \(M\) admitting an Anosov flow must have exponential growth, and \(M\) must be universally covered by \(\mathbb{R}^{3}\). Nevertheless, there are sufficient mechanisms for constructing distinct Anosov flows on admissible 3-manifolds, such as Dehn-Goodman-Fried surgery or playing with hyperbolic building blocks.
